/bin/sh -lc "python - <<'PY'
import json, os, tempfile
with open('/spec/formal-context.json') as f:
    source=json.load(f)
result={
 'schema_version':1,
 'candidate_hash':source['candidate_hash'],
 'status':'complete',
 'statement':'For every natural number n (including zero), real n by n matrices A and Rhat, and real u, if A is symmetric positive definite, 0 <= u, (n+1)u < 1, and Rhat is obtainable from the zero matrix by the specified relational execution of rounded upper-triangular entry computations, then DeltaA = Rhat"'^T Rhat - A is symmetric, Rhat''^T Rhat = A + DeltaA, and for all 0 <= i,j < n, |DeltaA[i,j]| <= ((n+1)u/(1-(n+1)u)) sum_{k=0}''^{n-1} |Rhat[k,i]| |Rhat[k,j]|. Successful execution is a hypothesis: the theorem does not assert that such an execution or output exists for every admissible A and u. The construction specifies possible results through real relative-error relations, rather than choosing a particular rounding rule.'"',
 'targets':[{
  'name':'Cholesky.cholesky_factorization',
  'statement':'Universally quantify n in the natural numbers, A,Rhat in R"'^{n x n}, and u in R. Write I_n = {0,...,n-1}. Assume A''^T=A, A is positive definite (x''^T A x > 0 for every nonzero real vector x indexed by I_n), 0 <= u, (n+1)u < 1, and SuccessfulCholesky(u,A,Rhat). Here SuccessfulCholesky means Execute(u,A,entryOrder(n),0,Rhat), with the zero matrix as initial state and the entry relations and order described below. Then there exists a real matrix DeltaA in R''^{n x n} such that DeltaA = backwardPerturbation(A,Rhat) = Rhat''^T Rhat - A, DeltaA''^T = DeltaA, Rhat''^T Rhat = A + DeltaA, and for every i,j in I_n, |DeltaA[i,j]| <= gamma(n+1,u) (entrywiseAbs(Rhat''^T) entrywiseAbs(Rhat))[i,j] = ((n+1)u/(1-(n+1)u)) sum_{k in I_n} |Rhat[k,i]| |Rhat[k,j]|. Products of matrices here are ordinary finite-sum matrix products, and n+1 in real arithmetic denotes its real coercion. No positive lower bound on n, existence of a successful run, or extra property of Rhat is an additional hypothesis.'"'
 }],
 'constructions':[
 {'name':'Cholesky.Rounded','description':'A predicate on u,exact,computed in R. Rounded(u,exact,computed) holds exactly when there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and computed = exact(1+delta). The definition itself imposes no separate assumption on u and chooses no delta or computed value. In particular, exact zero can only yield computed zero.'},
 {'name':'Cholesky.DotTail','description':'An inductively generated proposition DotTail(u,acc,xs,out), for real u,acc,out and a finite list xs of pairs of reals. Constructor nil: for every real u and acc, DotTail(u,acc,[],acc). Constructor cons: for every real u,acc,p,next,out,a,b and list xs, Rounded(u,a*b,p), Rounded(u,acc+p,next), and DotTail(u,next,xs,out) imply DotTail(u,acc,(a,b)::xs,out). Thus it represents a left-to-right accumulation from acc with a separately rounded multiplication and rounded addition for each pair. The intermediate values are witnesses to a relation, not outputs selected by an algorithm.'},
 {'name':'Cholesky.SequentialDot','description':'An inductively generated proposition SequentialDot(u,xs,out), for real u,out and a finite list xs of real pairs. Constructor nil: for every real u, SequentialDot(u,[],0). Constructor cons: for all real u,a,b,p,out and lists xs, Rounded(u,a*b,p) and DotTail(u,p,xs,out) imply SequentialDot(u,(a,b)::xs,out). The first product is rounded and used directly as the initial accumulator, with no addition to zero; each remaining product is rounded and then added with rounding by DotTail. These are constructors of a relation, not a deterministic dot-product function.'},
 {'name':'Cholesky.Residual','description':'A predicate Residual(u,row,a,dot,out) with u,a,dot,out in R and row in the natural numbers. If row=0 it requires exactly out=a and does not round a subtraction or constrain dot. If row is nonzero it requires Rounded(u,a-dot,out).'},
 {'name':'Cholesky.dotInputs','description':'For every natural n, real n by n matrix R, and i,j in I_n={0,...,n-1}, returns the finite list [(R[k,i],R[k,j]) : k=0,...,i-1], in increasing order of k. It filters the increasing list of all indices by k<i and maps each retained index to the indicated pair. There is no i<=j requirement in this definition.'},
 {'name':'Cholesky.writeEntry','description':'For every natural n, real n by n matrix R, i,j in I_n, and real value, returns the matrix whose (p,q) entry for every p,q in I_n is value if p=i and q=j, and R[p,q] otherwise.
